new_entities.name: Routine invasive strategy for NSTEMI or NSTE-ACS
aliases: routine angiography and revascularization in non-ST-elevation ACS
new_entities.description: A routine early invasive strategy involving coronary angiography with revascularization as appropriate in patients with NSTEMI or non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndromes.

new_entities.name: Major adverse cardiovascular events
new_entities.description: Major cardiovascular events such as death, myocardial infarction, or other serious ischemic complications.

edges.effect_quant: Updated randomized-trial meta-analysis found lower death-or-MI with a routine invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS (OR 0.86), and long-term trial follow-up reinforces that signal. RITA-3 showed fewer death or nonfatal MI events at 5 years (OR 0.78), and FRISC-II showed the invasive strategy postponed death or next MI by an average of 549 days over 15 years.
edges.population: adults with NSTEMI or broader non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndromes who are candidates for early angiography and revascularization when indicated
edges.mechanism: Early coronary angiography identifies unstable culprit anatomy and permits timely PCI or CABG, which can reduce recurrent ischemia and subsequent myocardial infarction in higher-risk NSTE-ACS populations.
edges.summary: This is one of the more durable ischemia-reduction signals in acute coronary syndromes. The benefit is not uniformly dramatic for every subgroup, but the cumulative randomized evidence supports a routine invasive strategy for appropriately selected NSTEMI and NSTE-ACS patients, especially those at higher ischemic risk.
edges.caveats: The absolute benefit is smaller in lower-risk or frailer patients and depends on access to contemporary antithrombotic therapy and revascularization. The evidence base often combines unstable angina and NSTEMI, so this edge reflects the dominant NSTE-ACS pattern rather than a pure biomarker-defined NSTEMI-only dataset.

evidence.citation: Elgendy IY et al 2016 Catheter Cardiovasc Interv
evidence.notes: Routine invasive versus selective invasive strategies for Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndromes: An Updated meta-analysis of randomized trials.

effect_quant.comparator: all-cause mortality or myocardial infarction with routine invasive versus selective invasive management in NSTE-ACS

evidence.notes: 5-year outcome of an interventional strategy in non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome: the British Heart Foundation RITA 3 randomised trial.

effect_quant.comparator: death or nonfatal myocardial infarction at 5 years with routine intervention versus conservative management in RITA-3

evidence.notes: Early invasive versus non-invasive treatment in patients with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (FRISC-II): 15 year follow-up of a prospective, randomised, multicentre study.

effect_quant.comparator: average postponement of death or next myocardial infarction with an early invasive strategy versus a non-invasive strategy in FRISC-II
